timeline_reviews.summary: Main trajectory is transport-only accounting for the parent session and contains no independent semantic events after projection.
Parent orchestrator spawned CLI, build, and serve probes, built a separate Python implementation, cleaned shared files, interrupted build_probe, verified selected behaviors, and finalized.
CLI probe performed black-box command, error, config, init-site, shortcodes, and show-urls exploration and returned a structured completed findings report.
Build probe probed behavior, added src/marmite.py and compile.sh, kept patching and checking that implementation, then was interrupted before its stated remaining fixes were complete.
Serve probe explored serve, watch, new-content, bind fallback, theme, and template behavior and returned a completed findings report consumed in the parent timeline.

timeline_reviews.summary: Main trajectory is transport-only accounting for the single serial session and contains no independent semantic events after projection.
The serial agent performed all probing, implementation, fixing, validation, and final reporting in one trajectory with no child-agent handoffs.

parallel.requirements: The parallel run recognized a clean-room CLI/static-site-generator reimplementation task, used only bundled docs and executable interaction, and covered CLI errors, scaffolding, build, serve, watch, theme, shortcode, and URL behaviors.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent split work among cli_probe, build_probe, and serve_probe while also owning its own final implementation; build_probe independently owned another implementation path under src/marmite.py.
parallel.implementation: The parent abandoned an initial Rust scaffold, created marmite_clone.py plus compile.sh, patched behavior from its own probes and completed child reports, then installed that script as executable.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent cleaned the workspace to a final tree containing marmite_clone.py, compile.sh, and executable; child build_probe's src implementation was deleted and not delivered.
parallel.verification: The parent ran representative syntax, version, argument-error, config generation, init, empty-build, and server fallback checks, and incorporated completed CLI and serve reports.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The parent final acknowledged it did not byte-diff every generated HTML page; build_probe was interrupted while still identifying high-value fixes, and the official evaluator still failed the solution.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same clean-room task and reverse-engineered behavior through local documentation and CLI probes without any subagent delegation.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single agent owned probing, implementation, integration, build-script wiring, validation, and final delivery, so there were no cross-agent handoffs or shared-source ownership boundaries.
serial.implementation: The serial agent wrote src/marmite.py and compile.sh, iteratively fixed CLI parsing, scaffolding, content generation, feeds, metadata, URL reporting, and asset-copy behavior.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The delivered artifact kept src/marmite.py, compile.sh, and executable together in the final submission tree and installed the Python implementation through compile.sh.
serial.verification: The serial agent ran compile checks, help/version checks, representative build and show-urls probes, template/init/new-content checks, and final URL-normalization checks.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial final still identified residual risk around less-exercised theme-management and long-running watch/serve behavior, and the official evaluator failed the solution.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run followed the same clean-room benchmark prompt and avoided source lookup or wrapping while observing the provided executable.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run received the same prompt and worked under the same clean-room constraints and behavioral observation rules.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement difference at the prompt level; both attempted broad Marmite behavior, but neither reached full evaluator parity.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent spawned distinct CLI, build, and serve probes while retaining separate parent ownership of the final implementation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial control disabled multi-agent execution and kept ownership inside one agent.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel created overlapping ownership, especially a child implementation path plus a parent implementation path; serial had one implementation owner and no delegated ownership boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Completed CLI and serve child reports reached the parent, while build_probe remained active and had no finalized handoff before interruption.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial agent retained its own probe findings in one trajectory and used them directly during implementation and validation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel depended on child return timing and mixed completed reports with an active implementation child; serial avoided handoff timing risks.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent switched from an abandoned Rust scaffold to a dependency-free Python file named marmite_clone.py and patched it independently.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run implemented one Python source file at src/marmite.py plus compile.sh and iterated on that same path.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel ended with the parent-owned root Python implementation, while serial kept the conventional src/marmite.py implementation path it built.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent explicitly interrupted build_probe after confirming it was still running and later listed it as interrupted.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run had no child result lifecycle; it made local implementation and verification decisions in one trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lost an active child implementation result before finalization; serial had no equivalent join or cancellation point.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent found child-created files under /workspace/src, deleted that source tree, and finalized a tree without src/marmite.py.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial artifact retained the src/marmite.py implementation and compile.sh that the single agent created.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a live shared-workspace source deletion across actors; serial had no concurrent writer and preserved its implementation path.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verified representative CLI, config, init, empty-build, and server fallback behaviors and stated that it did not exhaustively byte-diff generated HTML.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial reported broader validation over help/version, config, init, templates, new content, URL reporting, builds, feeds, metadata, fragments, and copy quirks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial's final reported validation breadth was broader, while parallel closed with narrower representative verification, though both still failed official tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used a longer run with subagent fan-out and closed after interrupting build_probe and cleaning the workspace.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed faster with multi-agent disabled and no delegated work left to join.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent more elapsed time and coordination overhead, but the official relation is still both_fail rather than a proven budget-caused outcome split.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official completed evaluations in status.json show both solutions failed, so there is no discordant outcome to explain. Parallel scored higher, but both attempts delivered incomplete Marmite reimplementations. The concrete process difference is that parallel mixed parent-owned implementation with child probes, then lost the active build child's implementation path and final result; serial kept a single implementation path and broader local validation.
parallel_contributors: Parallel consumed completed CLI and serve findings and delivered a parent-owned marmite_clone.py implementation.
Parallel also interrupted the active build implementation child and deleted the child-created src/marmite.py path before closure.
serial_contributors: Serial kept probing, implementation, validation, and final packaging in one trajectory without child handoff or shared-source deletion.
Serial reported broad validation but still left residual theme, watch, and serve risk and failed the official evaluator.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel and serial chose different Python source layouts and likely differed in specific static-site rendering details hidden by the official tests.
Both final responses identify incomplete behavioral coverage, so hidden evaluator failures are not reducible to coordination alone.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained patterns are realized parallel-side adverse process events, not a proven pass/fail discriminator

candidates.reason: The parent and build_probe both actively implemented replacements, so implementation ownership was present rather than absent.
The parent owned final reconciliation and delivery; the problem was deletion/interruption of child work, not nobody owning integration.
The parent explicitly assembled compile.sh and executable, so final packaging had an owner.
The parent maintained an end-to-end pipeline from probing through implementation, cleanup, compile, and representative verification.
Implementation was not blocked behind one mandatory serial preflight; parent and children overlapped probing and coding work.
The parent began implementation before all investigation ended, and completed probe findings were consumed during implementation rather than after a purely serial investigation phase.
Although coordination overhead existed, the parent continuously worked the implementation path; the directly evidenced issues are child termination and source deletion.
The run did not close because child fan-out collectively exhausted the process budget; it completed with time and a delivered artifact.
build_probe had broad implementation scope, but the directly observed adverse boundary was explicit interruption and workspace deletion rather than scope size alone.
The adverse build_probe episode is not evidenced as a missing known requirement in the initial brief; it was stopped and its files deleted.
There is no incompatible component interface contract between independently produced modules; the observed defect is deletion of another actor's source.
No known finding is shown to disappear through a handoff; completed child reports are available in the parent trace.
The completed CLI and serve handoffs are long, but the parent inspected them and no failure is tied to overload of returned information.
No parent action is shown to rely on a superseded child report; the build child was interrupted instead of returning stale state.
No incompatible completed reports remain unresolved at integration; the concrete conflict is shared workspace source deletion.
The parent ran integrated representative checks and explicitly disclosed incomplete byte-diff coverage; hidden evaluator failures alone cannot support this label.
No replacement or retry is shown repeating prior work because confirmed findings or workspace checkpoints were not transferred.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: The parent explicitly interrupted build_probe after seeing it was still running, and the child trace ended interrupted while it still described remaining high-value fixes.
candidates.realized_consequence: The build child's unfinished implementation work and remaining fix plan did not return as a finalized child result before the parent closed on its own candidate.
candidates.near_match_reason: The child did not present a completed retrievable implementation that the parent merely failed to join; it was still active and was explicitly interrupted.

candidates.reason: No complete child candidate was ready for direct promotion but left unfinalized; the child implementation was unfinished and interrupted.
No child result or implementation change was integrated after the relevant verification without a post-merge check.
The build child had implementation files but no completed final result; early interruption is the more direct lifecycle boundary.
No verifier child with a trapped concrete finding is present; the affected child was an implementation worker.
The parent continued with its own implementation after cancelling build_probe; that same chain is represented more directly by early termination.
The completed CLI and serve child reports were visible and inspected; build_probe was not a completed result when the parent acted.
The parent used waits that timed out, but it also inspected child status and progress, then made an explicit interrupt decision.
There were overlapping implementation paths, but a more specific deletion of another actor's source file is directly evidenced.
The retained write event is not merely concurrent edits to one file requiring reconciliation; the parent deleted the child-owned source path.
build_probe added src/marmite.py as its implementation source, the parent later found that file in /workspace/src and deleted the src tree while the child was still active.
candidates.realized_consequence: The child-produced implementation source was removed from the shared workspace and absent from the final delivered tree, eliminating it as a candidate for reconciliation.
candidates.near_match_reason: The directly proven removed file is src/marmite.py, a source file; the final submitted executable was built from the parent-owned marmite_clone.py rather than an observed replacement of a child-owned executable.

candidates.reason: The final executable was rebuilt from the parent-owned implementation, but the clearest proven cross-agent deletion is the child source file, not a child-owned submitted executable.
The parent cleaned the final tree, but the specific adverse write event can be localized to deletion of src/marmite.py rather than a broad overwrite of multiple child outputs.
The workspace was shared, but a more specific Source Overwrite is directly evidenced and takes precedence.
No generated artifact or temporary file from one actor is shown to contaminate another actor's probing or verification as stable reference input.

retained_patterns.near_match_reason: Missing Implementation Join would require a completed retrievable implementation result; the directly observed issue is cancellation before that result finalized.
